scope: Read-only control-quality audit of all four completed CodeGraph sessions. No model messages, reasoning, private task oracle, grader expectations, extra model queries or provider executions were inspected or invoked.

facts.statement: All eight official retrieval tools were configured and approved, matching the independent full-catalog qualification and frozen launch. This does not assert all eight were exercised in each run.
An isolated initial index was built for this exact workspace, with no prior state reuse, pending changes, pending references or worktree mismatch reported.
Recorded provider setup includes the initial indexing and readiness commands. No model query or extra MCP client ran during setup.
Returned excerpts match the completed workspace and independent integrity records show no protected source changes. Post-edit refresh was not exercised by these analysis sessions.
Native shell, source, compiler and package inspection remained available. Public commands show the agent used native follow-up rather than being restricted to graph evidence.
Capture and lifecycle receipts confirm the owned process groups and daemon stopped, with no remaining owned provider process.

sourceVerification.policy: Numbered source lines and import blocks are compared exactly at their returned locations. Signature fragments must match within their declaration first line; every subsequent fragment line matches exactly. This does not validate graph completeness or every relationship.

mcp.assessment: Successful bounded source and graph response. Explicit omissions are a provider response limit, not a harness truncation or setup error.

nativeFailures.classification: Agent-authored native script syntax error; not a CodeGraph transport error

runs.conclusion: No observed configuration, readiness, transport, source freshness or cleanup fault. Bounded retrieval and the agent choice of follow-up tools are distinct from setup defects.

limitations: This audit does not establish complete or semantically correct graph relationships, full task correctness, workflow adherence or comparative superiority. Separate frozen graders and action reviews address those questions.
The server reported a complete index; this is not independent proof that every language construct or repository file was indexed correctly.
Three explore calls disclose omitted relationships and source. The search call is discovery evidence. All eight tools were enabled, but only explore and search were exercised here.
These tasks did not modify production source. The earlier independent scratch qualification, bound separately, establishes an observed post-edit refresh only on that scratch project.
A generic unstable-features Codex warning remains in the public captures. No provider transport failure was observed.
The original confirmation001 stopped during common preparation before any provider or model session. It contributes no CodeGraph control result.

The study advertises the full eight-tool MCP configuration. A separate CLI-only configuration or affected-test workflow was not explicitly tested. This audit does not identify an optimal CodeGraph configuration.
